title: Coherence of the native tensor-forgetting comparison
statement: Given the native derived-square data, a comparison t satisfying the full representative square has a TensorCoherence witness for the transported native monoidal and symmetric structures. This isolates the transport of the associator, unitors, and symmetry equations from the representative-square construction.

source.place: Native tensor transport, geometric tensor part of step 3; Stacks 06YU, 0FPT

proof.text: Transport the four coherence equations of the supplied ringed TensorComparison through the native and ordinary localized equivalences. Use the representative square to identify the transported comparison with t, then cancel the comparison isomorphisms and use naturality to obtain associator, left and right unit, and symmetry equations.

proof_origin.place: Native tensor transport, geometric tensor part of step 3; split from the parent after the representative square was proved.

mathlib_searches.query: transport TensorCoherence through an equivalence of derived categories and identify a comparison by its representative square
mathlib_searches.results: No exact theorem matching the native and ordinary equivalence transport with the displayed representative-square normalization; the generic ringed coherence theorem is the closest interface.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No exact match; retain as a strict intermediate statement.

The existing NativeWeilTensorRingedTransport theorem contains the intended transport in a later module that imports the parent, so it cannot be imported here without a cycle.
